# Introduction

The anthropogenic climate crisis is a significant threat to global health [@vanDaalen2022].
The healthcare sector is responsible for an estimated 5–10% of greenhouse gas emissions [@Hu2021].
Fluorinated volatile anaesthetics such as sevoflurane and desflurane are a relevant source of these emissions [@Andersen2012; @Hu2021].
Furthermore, as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), they form persistent degradation products
that accumulate in aquatic ecosystems,
representing an environmental hazard beyond their global warming potential [@Kalmar2025b].

Activated charcoal canisters fitted passively at the exhaust port of the anaesthesia machine
can adsorb exhaled volatile anaesthetics and reduce their atmospheric release [@Wenzel2024;@Gibb2024b].
The CONTRAfluran^TM^ canister (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Luckenwalde, Germany)
is the only system currently approved in Europe for pharmaceutical reuse of recaptured sevoflurane.

Published evidence on the capture efficiency of CONTRAfluran for sevoflurane is limited.
Mulier et al. reported a canister weight gain of 45% during laparoscopic surgery
but did not quantify the capture efficiency of sevoflurane [@Mulier2024a].
Our preceding single-centre study found a capture efficiency of 34%,
with markedly different values in its two operating rooms
(21.4% and 47.8%) [@Gibb2025].

Single-centre studies are susceptible to site-specific bias
and the capture efficiency achievable on a larger scale therefore remains unknown.

Multicentre data could
improve generalisability
but remain lacking [@Gandhi2024].
We therefore conducted the first prospective, multicentre, international observational study
in Germany and Austria
to quantify the proportion of sevoflurane recaptured by CONTRAfluran under routine clinical conditions.
